oneLiner: A ~$3.9B option on solid-state batteries going commercial: four top-10 OEMs and standout safety data, against zero GAAP revenue, a $64M-per-quarter EBITDA burn, and a PowerCo program just capped at $75.4M.
thesis: Four of the top-10 global automakers are now engaged. Honda signed a multi-year partnership June 18, 2026 after one of the most rigorous evaluations of QS technology to date, joining VW's PowerCo and two other OEMs under joint development agreements; cells also shipped to an additional automotive OEM in Q2 2026.

The Eagle Line is finally ramping. Core tools ran above 90% uptime in Q2 2026 with productivity metrics on target; management aims to double cell output in H2 2026, with customer sample shipments accelerating across all three business verticals.

The licensing model is genuinely capital-light. FY2026 capex guidance was cut to $27-37M (July 2026) while $859M of liquidity against a $250-275M adjusted EBITDA loss guide gives roughly three years of runway before new equity is needed.

New verticals widen the funnel beyond autos. QSDC targets AI data center 800V rack power via ODM engagements, and QSAS shipped QSE-5 cells to a major American defense prime (Q2 2026); the anode-free design sidesteps China-sourced graphite entirely.

Safety is the wedge. Larger-scale Q2 2026 abuse testing -- nail penetration, external short circuit, thermal stability to 300C -- replicated earlier prototype results; the ceramic separator is nonflammable, a claim silicon-anode and liquid-electrolyte rivals cannot make.

latestProse: Q2 2026 (reported July 22): GAAP net loss $98.2M on $106.1M of opex; adjusted EBITDA loss $64.2M, in line. Customer billings of $10.8M brought H1 to $21.8M, already above all of FY2025 ($19.5M), though GAAP revenue remains essentially nil. Liquidity ended at $859.0M with Q2 operating cash use of $56.7M and capex of only $4.6M. The Honda partnership (June 18) added a fourth top-10 OEM, the Eagle Line hit >90% core-tool uptime with output set to double in H2, and QSAS shipped QSE-5 cells to a US defense prime. The disclosure that matters most: the July 16 PowerCo amendment, which swapped open-ended cost reimbursement for delivery-and-validation milestones over the next two years and capped total program payments at $75.4M including amounts already paid.
guidanceProse: FY2026 guidance: adjusted EBITDA loss of $250-275M reiterated; capex cut to $27-37M on capital discipline. There is no revenue guidance -- QS is pre-revenue at scale, and even customer billings carry a company disclaimer about quarter-to-quarter lumpiness. The central debate is what the amended PowerCo deal means: bulls note milestone payments tied to cell delivery and validation over the next two years keep VW on a defined path toward the IP License Agreement and its royalty prepayment; bears note $75.4M all-in is a rounding error against a $250M+ annual burn and looks like scope reduction. Second debate: whether QSDC/QSAS diversification is a real market or a narrative bridge while automotive validation grinds.
segments: QSEV (electric vehicles): PowerCo/VW licensing (prospective 40 GWh, expandable to 80 GWh annually), Honda partnership, and two other top-10 OEM joint development programs.
QSDC (AI data centers): battery solutions for 800V DC rack architectures via ODM design engagements; vertical stood up in Q2 2026 under ex-MediaTek executive Shahar Noy.
QSAS (aerospace/defense): QSE-5 cells shipped to a major US defense prime in Q2 2026; pitch is energy density, safety, and a China-free anode supply chain.
competitive: In-house OEM and Asian incumbent programs are the real competition: Toyota, Samsung SDI, and CATL are all driving sulfide-based solid-state toward late-decade production; if they industrialize first, licensing QS technology loses urgency.

Enovix (ENVX): silicon-anode cells already shipping commercially into smartphones from Fab2 in Malaysia -- nearer-term revenue with a similar energy-density pitch, but a flammable liquid electrolyte; QS's safety data is the counter.

Solid Power (SLDP): the closest business-model comp -- sulfide electrolyte plus licensing deals with SK On and BMW A-sample lines -- trading at a small fraction of QS's market cap, framing the premium QS must justify.

Tesla (TSLA) and CATL keep bending the conventional cost curve (4680, LFP, fast-charge chemistries). QSE-5's energy-density and safety edge must beat a $/kWh target that falls every year it stays pre-commercial.
moat: The ceramic separator plus anode-free lithium-metal architecture is protected by a deep patent estate and now backed by unusually strong third-party validation: four top-10 OEMs and replicated abuse-test safety data. What is unproven is everything industrial: Cobra separator yield at gigawatt-hour scale, cost per kWh versus falling lithium-ion prices, and whether B-sample cells survive automotive qualification into a production commitment. No customer has committed to mass production, and the PowerCo IP license -- the moat's monetization -- remains unsigned.
risks: The PowerCo amendment caps the program at $75.4M all-in. The July 16, 2026 restructuring replaced cost reimbursement with two years of delivery-and-validation milestones -- external funding covers well under half a year of burn, and the IP License Agreement remains unsigned.

There is no GAAP revenue. Customer billings ($10.8M in Q2 2026) are an invoicing metric the company itself warns is lumpy and not a substitute for revenue; commercial product revenue at scale is still years out.

Runway forces a raise before the payoff. $859M of liquidity against a $250-275M FY26 adjusted EBITDA loss guide is roughly three years; weighted shares already rose ~10% YoY, and QS has issued equity repeatedly since 2023.

Validation timelines have slipped before. QS went public in 2020 targeting mid-decade production; amended PowerCo milestones now run roughly through mid-2028 just for cell delivery and validation, with high-volume manufacturing later still.

Rival chemistries can close the gap. Toyota, Samsung SDI, and CATL sulfide solid-state programs target late-decade production while LFP and silicon-anode incumbents keep cutting $/kWh -- the premium QSE-5 must justify shrinks annually.
The market already voted on the quarter. QS fell roughly 31% in July 2026 into and after the print, with the Street reading the PowerCo restructuring as de-scoping rather than deepened commitment.
catalysts: H2 2026: Eagle Line output doubling and a step-up in customer sample shipments across QSEV/QSDC/QSAS.
PowerCo delivery-and-validation milestone payments over the next two years (amendment dated July 16, 2026; up to $75.4M aggregate).
Q3 2026 results (~late Oct 2026): billings cadence and any B-sample validation disclosures.
First QSDC data-center design win or QSAS defense program award (2026-2027).
Entry into the IP License Agreement with PowerCo and the associated royalty prepayment -- the single biggest de-risking event; timing undefined.
pricedIn: At about $6.30 (early Aug 2026), market cap is roughly $3.9B on 617M shares; net of $859M liquidity, EV is near $3.0B. Conventional multiples do not apply: GAAP revenue is nil and even billings annualize to only ~$43M, so the market is underwriting outcomes, not results. What is implied: QSE-5 completes validation, PowerCo signs the IP license, and royalties eventually flow across EV plus data-center and defense verticals -- effectively a modest probability on a very large licensing business. The debate: bulls see four top-10 OEMs and Honda's June 2026 endorsement as accumulating proof; bears see the 31% July drawdown, a capped PowerCo program, and three years of cash as a countdown clock.

scenarios.bear: B-sample validation slips again, PowerCo milestones stretch, and the IP license stays unsigned through 2027. QSDC and QSAS produce demos but no contracts, billings stagnate around $40M a year, and QS returns to the equity market in 2028 with the stock weak -- heavy dilution at low prices. The stock trades toward liquidity value, $2-3, as the market concludes solid-state arrives via Toyota and CATL rather than via licensing.
scenarios.base: The Eagle Line doubles output in H2 2026, PowerCo milestones pay on schedule through 2027-28, and Honda plus one more OEM deepen their programs. The IP license lands around 2028, triggering the royalty prepayment and a licensing framework; first gigawatt-hour-scale production follows early next decade. QS raises once more at tolerable dilution. The stock oscillates roughly $5-12 on milestone news -- still an option, but one whose strike keeps getting closer.
scenarios.bull: Safety plus energy density win a data-center or defense design commitment in 2027 -- revenue arrives years before automotive SOP. PowerCo signs the IP license with its royalty prepayment, Honda converts toward a licensing structure, and Cobra's larger-format separators unlock premium cell formats. Billings compound past $150M by 2028 while the licensing model holds capex under $40M a year. The market re-rates QS as an IP royalty company: $15-20.

valPresets.note: QS is pre-revenue at scale -- GAAP product revenue is nil, so 'revenue' here means licensing/prototype customer billings (~$43M annualized run-rate as of Q2 2026). Revenue mode compounds that base into prospective royalty streams; margins reflect an IP-licensing model, not cell manufacturing. Base (~45% CAGR to ~$780M by 2034) approximates a signed PowerCo license plus one additional licensee; bear is essentially liquidity value.
